content.focus_note: Watch to understand Tutorials concepts in SQL.

content.doc_md:
The CASE statement goes through conditions and return a value when the first condition is 
met (like an IF-THEN-ELSE statement). So, once a condition is true, it will stop 
reading and return the result.

If no conditions are true, it will return the value in the ELSE clause.

If there is no ELSE part and no conditions are true, it returns NULL.

The following SQL will order the customers by City. However, if City is NULL, then order by Country:

### Code Snippets

```
SELECT OrderID, Quantity,
CASE
WHEN Quantity > 30 
  THEN "The quantity is greater than 30"
WHEN Quantity = 
  30 THEN "The quantity is 30"
ELSE "The quantity is 
  under 30"
END
FROM OrderDetails;

---

CASE
WHEN
condition1
THEN
result1
WHEN
condition2
THEN
result2
WHEN
conditionN
THEN
resultN
ELSE
result
END;

---

SELECT CustomerName, City, Country
FROM Customers
ORDER BY
(CASE
WHEN City IS NULL THEN Country
ELSE City
END);
```
